event: Helium flash at the RGB tip
Core helium exhausted; AGB ascent begins
notes: Degenerate C-O core with H and He shells burning above it.

event: AGB tip: ~3000 L-sun, brighter than the RGB tip
notes: Reached in ~20 Myr rather than 0.6 Gyr. Hotter than the RGB tip (~3000 K) so physically smaller, ~200 R-sun.
Each pulse a few hundred years. Dredge-up carries carbon, nitrogen and s-process elements to the surface.

event: Superwind: mass loss at 10^-5 to 10^-4 solar masses per year
notes: Whether the Sun becomes a carbon star (C/O > 1) is at the edge of models. Sackmann et al. 1993.
Above 100,000 K, Earth-sized, several thousand L-sun almost entirely in the UV.
Oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen emission lines. Shells within shells, structured by the thermal pulses that drove them off.

event: Nebula thins past visibility and disperses
notes: Carries dredged-up carbon, nitrogen and metals into the interstellar medium.

event: White dwarf at peak output: ~15 L-sun, ~0.5 solar masses
notes: ~5% of today's sunlight in the visible; the rest extreme UV. 25 arcseconds across. Anything once at 1 AU is now near 2 AU.

event: Cooling well underway; surviving outer planets frozen
Core crystallizes; latent heat briefly stalls cooling
notes: Oxygen crystallizes first and sinks, carbon floats. Confirmed by Gaia as a pile-up in the cooling sequence (Tremblay et al. 2019).
